//: AION SoC - LibreLane configuration template.
This file is never handed to LibreLane directly. scripts/prepare_librelane_config.py
resolves the source list from FuseSoC, rewrites paths relative to the run
directory, applies the '_modes' overlay for the requested target and writes
the result to <run dir>/config.json. The '//' and '_modes' keys are stripped
on the way out.
Targets:  make synth | make pnr | make pnr_simple
TinyTapeout compatibility
The floorplan half of this file reproduces what tt-support-tools generates
for a 4x2 ihp-sg13g2 tile, so a run here lands the same macro the shuttle
would build. TT composes two files -- the template's src/config.json and the
user_config.json that project.py's create_user_config() writes -- and merges
them; both are folded in here, with the differences called out where they
occur. The reference is
https://github.com/TinyTapeout/tt-support-tools/blob/main/project.py
https://github.com/TinyTapeout/ttihp-verilog-template/blob/main/src/config.json
Five keys of TT's src/config.json are deliberately absent, because this
LibreLane has no variable by those names and would only warn about them:
RUN_LINTER and LINTER_INCLUDE_PDK_MODELS lint Verilog, which a VHDL design
never produces before synthesis; RUN_CTS names a step, not a variable, and
OpenROAD.CTS is in the flow already; RUN_KLAYOUT_XOR and RUN_KLAYOUT_DRC are
TT's way of buying back CI minutes, and giving up the XOR and the KLayout
DRC is a bad trade for a design that is checked once rather than 300 times.
The *_VIOLATION_CORNERS lists are pinned rather than left to their
defaults. Setup and hold already covered every corner (setup via the
TIMING_VIOLATION_CORNERS fallback, hold via its own default), but max
slew and max cap default to [""], which LibreLane filters down to an
empty corner list -- so those two checkers examined nothing and still
reported 'No ... violations found'. The 'lenient' overlay empties all five.
//clock: The one TinyTapeout value this design has to change. TT's src/config.json
asks for 20 ns and says, in its own comment, to increase it if setup fails.
It does, and not by a little: the worst path runs from an operand register
in aion_interface through the whole posit ALU to uo_out -- 121 cells, no
register anywhere in it -- because aion_interface.vhd drives uo_out
combinationally from `result` for addresses 0x5 and 0x6. The SDC budgets
IO_DELAY_CONSTRAINT (20%) of the period at each end, so that path gets
0.8 * period minus 0.25 ns of uncertainty, and at 20 ns it missed by 3.091
Raising the period is not free arithmetic, because synthesis targets it too:
at 30 ns the netlist came back slower (arrival 18.841 -> 25.602 ns) and the
path still missed by 1.852. 40 ns is the measured value that closes.
The fix that would buy the speed back is in the RTL, not here: register
`result` before the read mux and the ALU leaves the output path entirely.
`done` already rises two cycles after `start`, so nothing reads the result
in the same cycle it is computed -- the combinational path is not one the
//floorplan: A plain 350 x 200 um box. This macro is not hardened as a TinyTapeout tile
any more -- it is hardened to be instantiated, twice, in a top level that
lives in another repository, so TT's DIE_AREA and its DEF template (which
pins all 43 pins to the north edge for the multiplexer) would both be the
wrong shape. implementation/def/tt_block_4x2_pgvdd.def is kept in case the
TT floorplan is wanted again; set LIBRELANE_DEF_TEMPLATE to re-enable it.
Pin placement therefore falls back to implementation/pin_order.cfg, which
spreads the pins over all four sides -- what you want for a macro a parent
has to route to from an arbitrary direction.
What is kept from TinyTapeout is everything that is a *rule* rather than a
floorplan: the tt_um_* port list including ena, the VPWR/VGND supply names,
and the layer restrictions under '//routing' below.
//power: VPWR/VGND are the names the harness's DEF declares in its SPECIALNETS, and
PDN_MULTILAYER off is TT's 'don't generate power rings'. TT spells the last
two FP_PDN_VPITCH and FP_PDN_MULTILAYER, which this LibreLane accepts as
deprecated aliases; the current names are used here so the run does not
//routing: The layer rules TinyTapeout imposes, which outlive its floorplan.
RT_MAX_LAYER is tech.py's project_top_metal_layer for ihp-sg13g2: a project
may route up to TopMetal1 and no further. PDN_MULTILAYER off is the other
half of the same rule -- PDN_HORIZONTAL_LAYER defaults to TopMetal2 for this
PDK, and tt-support-tools' precheck lists TopMetal2.drawing among its
forbidden layers, so a project GDS carrying any is rejected. Leaving these
two alone is what keeps the macro submittable.

//: Overlays merged on top of the base configuration by
scripts/prepare_librelane_config.py. 'lenient' is applied last and is
enabled with LENIENT=1 on any make target.
PnR from a pre-existing netlist that may instantiate AI-generated cells.
RSZ_DONT_TOUCH_RX is deliberately left at its default ('$^', matches
nothing). Setting it to '^_AION_.*' marks every AI cell instance
don't-touch, and OpenROAD then refuses to insert a fanout buffer in
front of ANY of their input pins -- repair_design aborts with
RSZ-3006 on the first high-fanout net that feeds one. 46 of the
netlist's 65 nets with fanout > MAX_FANOUT_CONSTRAINT drive an AI
cell, so this is not a net the flow can route around.
The cells do not need the protection: their liberty functions are
4-input fusions with no equivalent in sg13g2, so the resizer has
nothing to swap them for, they are neither buffers nor inverters, and
DESIGN_REPAIR_REMOVE_BUFFERS is false. Confirm they survived by
grepping the hardened netlist -- flow/7_pnr/nl/tt_um_aion.nl.v --
for the AION_ masters after a run.
Downgrade every hard checker so a broken custom cell still yields a
GDS and a full set of reports to look at. Never use for signoff.
